title: How do we add the numbers in a picture two ways?
description: Two grids of numbers are added by shape or by number, and again by rows. Equal numbers are grouped, and a shared multiplier is written once outside a bracket.
teaching_notes: One idea: count equal numbers as groups, or add the rows, and both ways give the same total. Watch for students who add every cell in the grid as if it showed the same number.

video_script.why: The child adds the numbers in a picture in two ways and writes each way as an expression.
video_script.substitution: Group equal numbers and write one product for each group, or add each row and then add the rows.
video_script.anchor: Two grids of numbers: a three by three grid of fours and eights, and a four by four grid of fives and sixes
video_script.payoff_line: Picture one totals fifty two and picture two totals eighty eight.

final_answer.spoken: picture one totals fifty two and picture two totals eighty eight

never_show: a grid cell with a number that is not in the picture
maths_rules: picture I has 5 squares showing 4 and 4 circles showing 8
by rows: top and bottom rows are 4 + 8 + 4 = 16, the middle row is 8 + 4 + 8 = 20
picture II has 8 cells showing 5 and 8 cells showing 6
by rows: two rows are 5 + 6 + 6 + 5 = 22, two rows are 6 + 5 + 5 + 6 = 22, and 4 × 22 = 88
video_script.design: One idea: group equal numbers or add rows, and both ways agree. Uses the method of the solved example on adding equal lots. The two grids stay on the board all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about adding numbers in a picture.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>Picture one is a three by three grid with fours and eights.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>Picture two is a four by four grid with fives and sixes.
<bookmark mark='h4'/>How can we add the numbers in each picture in two different ways?

beats.on_screen: both pictures stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: four circles each marked 8 grouped into one lot of 4 times 8; one row of cells added left to right

marks.g1: the four circles slide together into one group
marks.g2: the group is written as four times eight
marks.g3: one row is added from left to right

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>When many cells show the same number, we count them as a group.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Four cells of eight are four times eight.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>We can also add each row, and then add the rows.

beats.on_screen: Given: picture I has 5 squares of 4 and 4 circles of 8; picture II has 8 fives and 8 sixes

marks.gv1: the contents of picture one are written
marks.gv2: the contents of picture two are written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, picture one has five squares of four and four circles of eight.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>Picture two has eight fives and eight sixes.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum of each picture in two ways, with an expression for each way

marks.fd1: the words two ways and an expression are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find each sum in two ways, and write an expression for each way.

marks.s11: picture one is shown grouped by shape

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, picture one, by shape.
There are five squares of four and four circles of eight.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>The total is five times four plus four times eight.
<bookmark mark='s13'/>That is twenty plus thirty two.

beats.on_screen: picture I by rows: top and bottom 4 + 8 + 4 = 16; middle 8 + 4 + 8 = 20; 2 × 16 + 20 = 32 + 20

marks.s21: the top and bottom rows are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, picture one, by rows.
The top and bottom rows each read four plus eight plus four, which is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>The middle row reads eight plus four plus eight, which is twenty.
<bookmark mark='s23'/>The total is two times sixteen plus twenty, which is thirty two plus twenty.

marks.s31: the fives are outlined in one colour and the sixes in another
marks.s33: the common 8 moves outside a bracket and 8 × 11 appears

beats.colours: fives in one colour, sixes in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, picture two, by number.
Eight cells show five, and eight cells show six.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>The total is eight times five plus eight times six.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>The eight is common, so it is eight times open bracket five plus six close bracket.
That is eight times eleven.

beats.on_screen: picture II by rows: 5 + 6 + 6 + 5 = 22 and 6 + 5 + 5 + 6 = 22, so 4 × 22

marks.s41: two rows are outlined and their total 22 appears
marks.s42: the other two rows are outlined and their total 22 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, picture two, by rows.
Two rows read five plus six plus six plus five, which is twenty two.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>The other two rows read six plus five plus five plus six, which is also twenty two.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>The total is four times twenty two.

beats.on_screen: check: 20 + 32 and 32 + 20 use the same numbers; 8 × 5 + 8 × 6 = 40 + 48 and 4 × 22 = 80 + 8

marks.s51: the two ways of picture one are placed side by side
marks.s52: 40 + 48 and 80 + 8 are placed side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='s51'/>Step five, check that the two ways agree.
Twenty plus thirty two and thirty two plus twenty use the same two numbers.
<bookmark mark='s52'/>Eight times five plus eight times six is forty plus forty eight.
Four times twenty two is eighty plus eight. The two totals are the same.

marks.a2: the two expressions are written beside the totals

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Picture one totals fifty two and picture two totals eighty eight.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Each picture gives the same total in both ways.
